depth: In frames 1–2, the depth map captures an indoor cafe layout with a standing woman on the far left out of reach (~3–5 m, bright white), a seated man in the center-right (~2.5 m) with a menu out of his reach, a seated woman in front and to his left (~0.5–1.2 m, ~1.5 m from him) holding a menu, a pastry case on the far right (~2.0 m), and two tall beverage refrigerators along the back wall (~0.5–1.5 m). segmentation: In frames 1–2, the segmentation map outlines the refrigerator on the right-center (merging both units in frame 1 and missing the left unit in frame 2) containing a few small bottle masks, the seated man in front of it (~2.5 m), the seated woman in front of him to the left (~0.5–1.2 m) above a partially occluded chair mask, and the far woman partly out of view on the left edge (~3–5 m). The segmentation map provides crisp object-level silhouettes and isolates individual bottles inside the fridge and small tableware far from the counter that blend into the cluttered RGB foreground. However, it is unreliable under motion blur in frame 3, misclassifies the glass pastry display case as a 'tv' in frames 4–5, drops the second refrigerator in frame 2, and fails to segment the paper bag, menus, tables, and right-side display case.
pose: In frame 1, the pose map detects the upper-body skeleton and facial keypoints of the seated man (~2.5 m, center-right) facing and looking away from the camera wearer with his left hand raised, alongside the facial keypoints and single arm of the far woman on the left (~3–5 m) who faces right and slightly away from the camera; in frame 2, both the seated man (now looking down at his menu with both hands lowered out of reach of the table) and the far woman look downward, and the woman's skeleton is completely missed while the nearby seated woman in the foreground (~0.5–1.2 m) is never detected. In frame 3, no skeletons are detected at all due to severe motion blur and partial view of the people at the right and left frame edges. In frames 4–5, facial keypoints and a shoulder-and-arm skeleton track the man in the red shirt directly in front of the camera wearer as he moves away from ~3 m to ~5 m, showing his torso facing away while his head angles slightly downward toward the counter space between them in frame 5. The pose map makes body orientation, head pitch, and arm geometry explicit—such as the seated man's transition from an upright gesture in frame 1 to leaning over the table in frame 2, and the standing man's downward gaze and lowered arms in frame 5—without visual distraction from clothing or lighting. However, it is unreliable across the sequence because it outputs no magenta hand skeletons in any frame, misses the foreground woman in frames 1–2 and the background woman in frame 2, fails completely in frame 3, and reduces the man's torso in frame 4 to a single horizontal shoulder line due to lower-body cropping.
